correctness.rationale: A length-L word is specified by its initial bit and zero, one or two change locations; constant extension realizes each and the count is L²−L+2. At any fixed observation scale, uniform continuity of the quotient gives a word radius R. Equal unordered sets of words on [−R,N−1+R] give small Hausdorff orbit distance in both directions, even if representative multiplicities differ. Thus s_N=O(N^(2n)), and a continuous factor gives the same upper bound after singleton collapse. For a matching lower bound, use 2n successive windows of lengths proportional to N on one coarse grid of spacing larger than the fixed observation radius, pair successive windows for the two transitions of each finite 1-block, and choose one time in each window. At a differing passage time one configuration has a step marker separated from p and the other has only points near p. Every nonpassing point in the first configuration is also near p. For n≥2 the passing configuration is near {p,u} or {p,v}, whose suspension images are distinct from the collapsed singleton point. Uniform continuity supplies a fixed positive separation after collapse. This produces Ω(N^(2n)) choices at a fixed scale and handles n=1 before collapse. Closed inclusion of each F_n in the full hyperspace gives infinite polynomial entropy there; the finite-layer bound gives zero topological entropy at every scale. The recurrent context also checks independently: all nonconstant points are homoclinic to p and admit a transition cylinder that never returns (a specified transition type can occur only once); pseudo-orbits can jump between their two tails near p. Pairs of opposite steps are nonwandering in F_2: approximate each by a long block that first displays the designated step and then, at a common late time, displays the opposite member's step. The unordered pair returns arbitrarily near itself. Varying their locations gives infinitely many such configurations.
residual_risks: The finite symbolic replay tests marker combinatorics, not metric quotient topology or arbitrary n and N; those use the analytic separation and upper bound.
The suspension requires n≥2. No full-hyperspace topological entropy claim or arbitrary chain-recurrent classification was reviewed.

value.rationale: The same basic test system lies outside the finite-chain-recurrence multiplicativity theorem. Exact entropy at all finite levels, including survival of 2n independently observable passage times after collapse, settles a natural boundary case. It exhibits unbounded polynomial complexity across zero-topological-entropy finite layers. The key significance is the exact growth and robust collapsed-layer detection, not merely applying a factor inequality or calculating word counts.
residual_risks: No universality for compact systems with singleton nonwandering set, or for arbitrary quotients, follows from this example.
